subject.title: fix(sqlite): stop mount probes blocking database startup

question: Should database startup eliminate the fallback `mount` subprocess, or may it retain a synchronous one-second timeout with residual child-termination risk?
rationale: The current implementation improves ordinary hangs but cannot establish the stated no-blocking guarantee; accepting that residual availability risk and the new rollback threshold requires explicit SQLite-owner judgment.

options.title: Remove the startup subprocess
options.body: Use conservative rollback journaling when proc/statfs classification is unavailable so database opening never waits on an external command.

options.title: Accept the residual risk
options.body: Keep the one-second synchronous probe only with explicit owner acceptance and supported-host proof documenting the remaining child-termination and journal-mode behavior.

recommendation.title: Remove the startup subprocess
recommendation.body: Use conservative rollback journaling when proc/statfs classification is unavailable so database opening never waits on an external command.
